title: A small temporal cohort checks machine-learning estimates of dental pain
summary: A random-forest model estimated severe pain after third-molar extraction. Its AUC fell from 0.879 in internal evaluation to 0.724 in 38 later procedures, illustrating the limits of the initial result. The study does not establish improved pain management or independent-site validation.
ai_technology: LASSO feature selection and random forest

source_review.scope: Primary article full-text bibliographic metadata and relevant computational evaluation Methods/Results: sec2.7, sec2.8, sec3.3.

evidence.ai_role: LASSO feature selection and random forest fitted the represented classification or candidate-selection model; preprocessing and expert reference labels are distinguished from the learned contribution.
evidence.tested: The study included 185 patients and 202 procedures. Models were developed using 164 procedures from 2022 and evaluated on 38 procedures from 2023; five features were selected by LASSO.
evidence.unknown: Seventeen patients contributed another contralateral procedure; patient overlap across development and temporal sets is not established. Feature selection isolation and model locking before later outcomes accrued are not demonstrated, so this is a retrospective/temporal check. A November 2024 erratum corrects author order, not the represented measurements.
